title: Solvation closure of the Continuum Lab ion experiment (model steps 4–6), with the confined-mobility ratio (steps 5–6)
summary: Recorded CP2K first-shell counts and shell radii, literature hydration energies and stated example values give the excess free energy of each ion in the pore. Executable and labelled illustrative: it is not an ion-transfer free energy from molecular simulation, and it is not calibrated against a molecular or experimental conductance.

closures.name: Dehydration with the recorded CP2K first-shell counts
closures.formula: ΔG_i = (1 − κ_i) (N_lost,i / n_ref,i) ΔG_1,i, N_lost,i = max(0, n_ref,i − n_i)

closures.name: Dehydration with the rigid-shell geometry
closures.formula: as cp2k, with n_i = n_ref,i × fraction of a spherical shell of radius r1 that fits inside the water-accessible radius

closures.name: Dielectric exclusion (Born)
closures.formula: ΔG_i = N_A z_i² e² / (8π ε0 a_B,i) (1/ε_p − 1/ε_b)

conventions.profile: ΔG_i s(x): a smooth step of width 0.15 nm at each mouth
conventions.concentration_definition: moles per ion-accessible volume, averaged over the cross-section
conventions.note: The electrostatics of the rims and of the ions is in Poisson’s equation, not in ΔG, so it is not counted twice.

comparison_only.reason: single-file water: the continuum description is outside its domain; the page computes this tube for comparison only and flags it

validation.numerical_status: Solver and controller tests I1–I17 and IB1–IB11 (the page’s Validation section)
validation.note: The recorded-shell and rigid-shell closures give different currents for the same pore; the page computes the ratio for its default settings (“How molecular simulation enters the prediction”). The difference is a sensitivity of the prediction to the closure, not a validation of either.
